HRA Analysis: OVERVIEW:DUSTY PHILTRA (8) has significantly the best sectional times. Two starts ago, he finished second behind Enjoy Life in a Vicbred Super Series heat after flying home late. He has brilliant point-to-point speed. The barrier is a bit awkward, though, and he’s first-up since early September. HELLO POSSUMS (3) was below his best last start at Kilmore but went on to trial okay at Melton. If we ignore his last start, his runs prior were good. He was held up badly the start before that and, prior to that, he flashed home nicely into second. If he can map well, he will be flashing home late. DONMARO (10) is a nice horse at his best, but he looks to have had a few issues since arriving in Australia and we are yet to see the best of him. He comes into this race with a claim price. If he can turn his form around and bring his best, he will be a threat here. There are just a few question marks. MYSTIC MOTIVER (5) was a good winner at this track last start. This is harder, but he’s in form. CAPTAIN LOCKSLEY (1) is also worth respecting. He is a lightly raced horse who is third-up here, having had only four career starts. He ran second last start to Plutophobia. His win on debut was strong, racing in the breeze, and he looks like he can race tough. Barrier one suits, but this is his toughest test. BACK: DUSTY PHILTRA (8) – 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: DUSTY PHILTRA (8), HELLO POSSUMS (3), DONMARO (10), MYSTIC MOTIVER (5)

OVERVIEW:TOPHUT JOHNY (5) ran home well for fourth last start in a tougher race than this one. He rarely runs a bad race. If he can map well, he is a winning chance. James Herbertson takes the reins here. CARUSO STAR (4) got well back but ran home well last start at Cranbourne. He has the best sectional times in this event. He will need a little luck from the barrier. ARCHAA (2) is at his best when he is able to find the fence. He has good gate speed and should be able to map well here. HURRICANE HOOLY (8) is a consistent mare of late. She has been racing tough recently and performing okay. The barrier is awkward, but she’s performing well. BACK: TOPHUT JOHNY (5)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: TOPHUT JOHNY (5), CARUSO STAR (4), ARCHAA (2), HURRICANE HOOLY (8)

OVERVIEW:ATEGO DAWN (9) was good winning first-up last start at Cranbourne. She was able to hold the front and lead all the way. From barrier nine, she can follow through and get into a good position in the running line. She has the winning confidence. CHINSKI (6) got tired trying to hold the front in a tougher contest last start. He is a nice horse at his best. If he can slot into a good position and be saved for one run, he should be hitting the line well late. DESERT ROYALE (10) has had two starts this time in. He broke when first-up and last start he got shuffled back late and lost his momentum. He does have some ability, but he will potentially need to make his own luck from the barrier. TARENTAISE (1) has been below his best in his last two starts. Last start, he was first-up in Victoria, where he gave ground and was vetted afterwards. He has since trialled okay. He has good gate speed and can map well. Also respecting BUMPER SERVICE (5) here. SELECTIONS: ATEGO DAWN (9), CHINSKI (6), DESERT ROYALE (10), TARENTAISE (1)

OVERVIEW:COGNAC COWBOY (2) is a lightly raced gelding who has only had five career starts. His three starts back this campaign have all been really good runs. Last start, he raced in the breeze and finished third, but it was a good run. He should be able to find the fence here and have a change of luck. THE PRIVATE DEAL (8) has the best sectional times in this field. Last start, she finished third after settling back in the field from barrier ten, covering ground wide and flashing home well late. Barrier eight is a bit awkward for her. SHESABITSALTY (9) is a first starter for Jess Tubbs. She looked like she was running home okay in a recent trial but wasn't pushed. We will learn more about her here. BAD GRANDMA (3) has only had three career runs for two fourths and a third. She doesn't seem to have good gate speed yet and has been getting well back before letting down nicely late. BACK: COGNAC COWBOY (2)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: COGNAC COWBOY (2), THE PRIVATE DEAL (8), SHESABITSALTY (9), BAD GRANDMA (3)

OVERVIEW:SHINELIKETHESUN (5) is an interesting trotter that you need to take on trust. She can get her manners wrong, but when she trots well, she has a lot of ability. She trotted throughout last start and was too good after racing in the breeze. If she does everything right, she can win again. MOONSHINE LOUIE (8) rarely runs a bad race. He hasn’t been out of the top four in his last 10 starts. He finished second to SHINELIKETHESUN (5) last start after making a run from well back. ALDEBARAN MISTIQUE (4) led that same race and just got a bit tired late last start. The start prior, she galloped. At her best, she is a nice mare and, if saved for one run here, can be quite competitive. KYVALLEY REEVA (9) is a nice filly when she trots. Last start, she got shuffled back but stormed home for second. She galloped the start prior but won her two starts before that. She has the class if she trots throughout. BACK: SHINELIKETHESUN (5)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: SHINELIKETHESUN (5), MOONSHINE LOUIE (8), KYVALLEY REEVA (9), ALDEBARAN MISTIQUE (4)

OVERVIEW:TED (7) is a former New Zealand pacer. He had one start in Australia last year, which was an impressive victory, but then he didn’t race for over a year. He’s returned with two okay runs recently. Last start, he raced in the breeze in a tougher race than this one and was only beaten 5 metres. He should improve again here with race fitness. POSTERIZED (1) is a smart gelding who performs well when he is in front. There is a lot of speed to his outside, so if he gets crossed, he should still get a good fence trip. STORM VENDETTA (5) is a smart gelding in good form. However, last start he did give punters a bit of a fright when he led at short odds and was nearly run down late. With his class, the win probably should have been easier for him. He can win this at his best, but there are just a few question marks about where he is at. ANGELS WATCHING (3) is a good sit sprinter who rarely runs a bad race. If he gets a good trip here, he will be one to watch late. BACK: TED (7)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: TED (7), POSTERIZED (1), STORM VENDETTA (5), ANGELS WATCHING (3)

OVERVIEW:NEW YORKER (7) is a smart horse at his best. He has a few quirks with his manners early, so he can get well back and need to make up ground late. At his best, he could make his own luck here. He needs to settle early and, although the barrier is tricky, he is a quality horse. FERRIGNO (4) was a solid sixth last start in a race won by the talented Cardigan Dan. His start prior was a good second at Melton after sitting in the one-one. He is racing consistently well and should perform strongly here. ROM BARO (5) is in fantastic form, winning four of his last six. He also recently contested the Vicbred Super Series, where he made the final, as well as the Victoria Derby. He is a quality horse but has a sticky barrier here. LOU WILL (2) has been racing well. He has good gate speed and, with a positive barrier here, should be able to find the fence. Also noting MISTER HUNTER (6), who was a brilliant Group 1-winning juvenile. He is second-up after a few years on the sidelines. He’s on his comeback campaign and may need a few runs to get race fit. SELECTIONS: NEW YORKER (7), FERRIGNO (4), ROM BARO (5), LOU WILL (2)

OVERVIEW:WALKING ON WATER (1) is an interesting pacing-bred trotter. He was in good form, finishing second in four of his last five starts, until last start when he paced and galloped. He gets the ace barrier here and should get a good run, but he needs to bring his best manners. That is a bit of a risk, given he paced last start. SYNTAX ERROR (3) raced in the breeze and tired late last start. Doing work in his runs is likely not his go. His runs prior were consistently okay, rarely finishing outside the top five. If saved for one run here, he may find a race to break through for his maiden victory. GYM QUEEN (4) galloped last start but is quite competitive at this grade when she puts it all together. Her start prior was good. She worked forward and found the front from barrier 11. She just got out-sprinted late after having to do some work in rain-affected conditions. She’s a winning chance with some luck. OVER HERE (2) ran home okay after getting well back from barrier six last start. He should be closer to the top here from barrier two and is an each-way chance. DANCE WITH ROXY (5) is another one to watch who seems to be putting it all together recently. She has gate speed. SELECTIONS: WALKING ON WATER (1), SYNTAX ERROR (3), GYM QUEEN (4), OVER HERE (2) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

BACK YA TRUCK UP (2) will look to reverse the result from his debut last start by making the most of drawing inside MYSTERY MAIL (3) this time around. They both performed well in quick time, putting a gap on their rivals. KOOKY (4) brings a different form line to those two, having been competing against the fillies, but seems to be getting better with each run, including last start when doing all the work mid-race in a fast mile rate and battling on well for second. Tactics will be interesting here, as she does possess sharp gate speed when asked. VINJETTA (1) continues to run handy races and earn nice cheques for her connections and will do similar here in the small field, but will need to improve on previous efforts to be a chance of knocking off the favoured runners. Selections:BACK YA TRUCK UP (2), MYSTERY MAIL (3), KOOKY (4), VINJETTA (1)

CRAYONS TO PERFUME (7) looks a handy 4yo mare still on the rise and looks the one to beat again here, despite drawing the outside front-row gate. It will be interesting to see whether connections push the button from out wide and look to assert her dominance, with some good gate speed drawn inside her. SWIATEK LEIS (6) is second-up from a long break and was dominant in winning all three Sires features throughout her juvenile years. It's hard to gauge where she's currently at, but if anywhere near her best, she looks the obvious danger. IM BUTTER BLUE (5) is an interesting runner who has been racing around the Riverina and possesses good gate speed when asked, while GOT THE GLOW (1) will no doubt be looking to kick through early and hold a forward position if she's on her best behaviour. She has put together two strong wins of late, albeit rising in class here. MOVESLIKEALADY (8) will be reliant on the tempo but will no doubt be flashing home late, as she normally does. The remaining runners have been consistent of late but rise in class here, and it's hard to see them finishing on the podium. Selections:CRAYONS TO PERFUME (7), SWIATEK LEIS (6), GOT THE GLOW (1), IM BUTTER BLUE (8)

BARNABY (1) resumes here off a handy trial and looks extremely hard to beat from the pole draw. Expect him to go around in red figures here, despite being first-up from a break. ATOMIC BLACK (5) and IDEN LADY LINCOLN (6) have both been in great form of late and are normally driven on speed, so may look to employ similar tactics again here from their wider front-row draws. DIDYALOUSAROOSTA (2) again gets the nice gate to be earning a cheque for his connections, as he usually does, while you would suspect the remaining runners will be battling it out for the minor cheques. Selections:BARNABY (1), ATOMIC BLACK (5), IDEN LADY LINCOLN (6), DIDYALOUSAROOSTA (2)

The first of the Youngbloods heats for the junior drivers, where the two-year-old filly in ANN PENNY (4) will again be taking on the older horses but looks to have enough ability to do so. Expect to see some good gate speed from those drawn inside her, including DENVER MAN (2) and GEMMY LOU (3), who are both capable of running a strong race on their day. JUST LIKA DREAM (5) will no doubt be another who attempts to find a forward position and always runs an honest race. CHEYS ANGEL (6) and OUR DANCE MONKEY (7) will be relying on some good tempo up front to allow them to run home strongly from their wide front-row gates, but both possess plenty of ability. HIGH FROSTY (1) could run a cheeky race from the pole draw if he doesn't gain a start in the Sires Final. Although he steps up in grade here, he can't be dismissed. Selections:ANN PENNY (4), DENVER MAN (2), OUR DANCE MONKEY (7), JUST LIKA DREAM (5)

ALWAYS BETTOR (4) will be looking to take advantage of the barrier draw over the other obvious main fancy in LIKEYOUFORAREASON (10). Both ran exceptional last halves in their heat two weeks ago and clearly look the yardsticks for the final here. The only query would be if IYLAC CHAMBER (2) was able to kick up early from the pole draw, should the emergency not gain a start, and decided to hold out ALWAYS BETTOR (4). It wouldn't surprise to see that happen off the strength of IYLAC CHAMBER (2) strong heat win when doing all the work in fast time and still proving too strong. Although the back-row draw hurts LIKEYOUFORAREASON (10), he clearly has plenty of ability, and his third placing in the Derby in August, when making a sustained wide run from the back of the field, showed he's capable of doing work from off the speed. PORT RUN MACHINE (8) could be the one at odds from the inside back-row draw off a hot tempo and clearly has plenty of ability when right. QUARTEIRA (6) possesses plenty of X-factor but draws an awkward gate here, which will make it tough for him, although he could be running home into the exotics. You would expect the remaining runners would need to improve to finish on the podium in what looks a classy Sires Final. Selections:ALWAYS BETTOR (4), LIKEYOUFORAREASON (10), IYLAC CHAMBER (2), PORT RUN MACHINE (8)

A ROCKIN NIGHTMARE (3) will look to take advantage of another handy front-row draw after being checked and subsequently breaking last start. Expect she may look to find the pegs ahead of the polemarker in KING BART (1), who does possess some gate speed when asked, before relinquishing the front to KENYA (5), who should ensure this race is run at an even tempo. He has been racing well but has found one too good on numerous occasions of late. CONSORT (6) draws wide on the front row and will look to slot in somewhere early, and with a nice run in transit, should be running home strongly. TWILIGHT BEACH (2) broke through for a deserving victory last start at big odds but rises slightly in grade again here, while the back-row runners will be relying on some good tempo throughout to allow them to run home strongly in what is one of many even fields on the card. Selections:A ROCKIN NIGHTMARE (3), KENYA (5), CONSORT (6), TWILIGHT BEACH (2)

The Group 3 Golden Apple Final over the 2,200-metre stand, where the two standouts in JACKS ULTIMATE FURY (10) and HORATIUS SPECULO (12) will look to do battle as they did in the heat and clearly look the class horses of the field, despite their backmark handicaps. JACKS ULTIMATE FURY (10) will again look to take advantage of starting off the 20-metre mark and stay ahead of his main danger early, attempting to employ similar tactics to when finding the front in the heat. However, I do expect the front-row horses may not hand up so easily this week, with standing-start veteran ROCKANDAHARDPLACE (5) likely to ensure they're running even quarters from the get-go, which may make it a tad tougher for those backmarkers this week. WAVES OF CHANCE (9) could be the one at odds off the 10-metre mark and clearly possesses plenty of ability when he switches on, whilst PADDO PLUGGER (1) could run a cheeky race from the pole, stripping fitter from his first-up run and being a normally handy beginner from the tapes. Selections:JACKS ULTIMATE FURY (10), HORATIUS SPECULO (12), WAVES OF CHANCE (9), ROCKANDAHARDPLACE (5)

The three-year-old Tasmanian fillies do battle in the Bandbox Final, and as expected following the prelude, it wouldn't surprise to see any runner bob up and take this out. TWILIGHT STORM (7) again draws wide on the front row, as she did in the prelude. However, expect she may have enough speed to find the pegs here, with STAYZBETTER (8) drawing the back row after galloping out last start. She cleared those inside her with some ease last time and would take plenty of running down if able to find the pegs. QUEEN ANASTASIA (4) was hard to miss when galloping on the final corner for no apparent reason before flashing home late to be narrowly beaten. If she puts her best foot forward here, she clearly looks one of the main dangers. MARIANA (3) was scratched from the prelude, so we are still none the wiser as to where her form sits amongst this field, but expect her to be in the finish if right. JILLSTIGER (2) enjoyed the even tempo when winning the prelude, and if able to replicate that performance from her nice draw here, she's another who clearly has the ability to take this out. QUETZALLI (1) will look to take advantage of the pole draw, while ASTORMZABREWEN (6) and STAYZBETTER (8) draw awkward gates and will need the right runs in transit to be finishing strongly. WILLOW STORM (9) was a strong maiden winner last start after only having fair form previously, and it wouldn't surprise to see her blouse them at big odds with further improvement. Selections:TWILIGHT STORM (7), QUEEN ANASTASIA (4), JILLSTIGER (2), MARIANA (3)

The lowest-class event of the night over the short distance, where COLORADO GIRL (2) should be first to the pegs before I suspect she may hand up to stablemate TUFFTIGER (3), who has been driven aggressively in all his starts for the stable thus far. BARBETTE (5) and FEELINKINDALUCKY (7) also possess good gate speed but may be driven more conservatively here from their wide gates, while JAY MILLER (6) will again look to sit on speed and try to out-tough them. Expect a strong tempo throughout, which should suit the back-row runners, where COOLANDCOLLECT (8) could be the one at odds from his soft trailing draw if gaps appear late, while DANCINWIVJOLENE (1) should again earn a cheque for connections from the pole draw. Selections:TUFFTIGER (3), JAY MILLER (6), COLORADO GIRL (2), COOLANDCOLLECT (8)

The final event of the night, which will also conclude the Youngbloods Series, looks very even on paper. There looks to be plenty of gate speed over the mile, with COUNTY COURT JUDGE (1) and INTO THE HARKNESS (2) looking to kick through hard early in an attempt to find a position on speed, while MISS COLLANN (5) possesses dazzling gate speed and may be better suited back to the mile this week. MUZZAME MATE (4) continues to run strong races and will again look to find a position on speed from his middle front-row draw and be hard to hold out late. MIKIYOURSOFINE (6) and MY WAY (7) are consistent pacers but expect they may have to be driven more conservatively here from their wide front-row draws. MR BONDI (10) and MONTGOMERY BURNS (11) appreciate the mile trip and will be relying on a good tempo throughout to allow them to run home strongly, while CALLING BUDDY (8) is an intriguing runner from Queensland. The market may be the best guide with him, but it wouldn't surprise to see him bob up if luck comes his way from the inside back-row draw. Selections:MUZZAME MATE (4), MR BONDI (10), COUNTY COURT JUDGE (1), MIKIYOURSOFINE (6) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

OVERVIEW: This is a competitive race to open the card, with a case that can be made for each horse. MONARO DEAN (3) is a former New Zealand trotter who has had just eight career starts, all from stand starts, for one victory. That win came early in his career over the 2600-metre trip on a grass track. On that occasion, he flashed home from the back of the field to win late. His last start in New Zealand was a second on the grass. He is now in the care of Andy Gath. He had a mobile trial at Melton, where he was slightly off the arm but got away okay. He won the trial by a big margin in slow time. He looks like a nice horse, but this is a very different style of racing to what he is used to. RAMBO SUFFARELL (4) is a better horse than his numerical form suggests. His last start was in March, when he got well back and flashed home nicely. His other prior runs were either unlucky or he got his manners wrong. He is first-up here, but he has some ability. FONDA RHONDA (10) has a nice turn of foot and can be a decent swooper late when saved for one run. Last start, she was first-up at Cranbourne and finished second after racing in the breeze for the last lap. Likely to improve again with fitness. SPIRITED GIGI (7) is a smart trotter who has raced competitively throughout his career against the top horses in his age group. A sticky barrier here. Also respecting the D’Arne Bellman-trained duo especially RAPTA (4).SHEZALOVER (9) and CHANTILLY LASS (2) are winning chances also. SELECTIONS: MONARO DEAN (3), RAMBO SUFFARELL (4), FONDA RHONDA (10), SPIRITED GIGI (7)

OVERVIEW:THE FASHIONISTA (10) has a strong last 800-metre sprint. She is first-up here for Andy Gath and finished second in a recent trial behind Coconut Mickey. Expecting a good performance here, but the wide back-row barrier is a concern. DREAMS OF LOVE (4) has been racing well and has found some of her best form since joining the Kaylene Ward stable. She won well after leading two starts ago at Ballarat and has since gone for a spell. At her best, she’s a winning chance here, although fitness will be a query. KALARNEY PRINCE (3) is a flashy grey trotter who is hard to miss. He doesn’t win often, but rarely runs a bad race. He will need to map well here for luck to be in his favour. ALLWATFUNJINGLES (1) has good gate speed and the ace barrier to use to his advantage here. BACK: THE FASHIONISTA (10)– 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS: THE FASHIONISTA (10), DREAMS OF LOVE (4), KALARNEY PRINCE (3), ALLWATFUNJINGLES (1)

OVERVIEW: This is another very competitive event with many winning chances. KYVALLEY DAYTONA (10) is having her third career start. On debut, she finished third at Maryborough after flashing home nicely. Last start, she got it wrong with her manners. Since then, she has won a slow trial at Kilmore. She looks to be a nice type when she puts it all together. TRUE APLOMB (3) is a well-bred filly who has promise but can get it wrong with her manners. Last start, however, she did everything right and finished second at Maryborough behind the smart Jilliby Connection. She chased determinedly there and gapped the other rivals behind her. DELIGHTFUL REYNA (1) has the best barrier she has had since early in her career. She has been racing okay, but with a positive race map here, she finds a chance to turn her form around. ALDEBARAN BOBBY (4) is a first starter for Jodi Quinlan. He let down well in a recent trial behind the older horse Night Flight. We will learn more about him here. BACK: KYVALLEY DAYTONA (10)– 2 units (win) SELECTIONS: KYVALLEY DAYTONA (10), TRUE APLOMB (3), DELIGHTFUL REYNA (1), ALDEBARAN BOBBY (4)

OVERVIEW:HIGHVIEW HAMMER (2) was an okay second last start when leading. He is first-up here for Samantha Gangell. He has fantastic gate speed and should be able to find the fence. SPORTS WRACK (6) is an experienced horse who is versatile and rarely runs a bad race. He got back into the winner’s circle two starts ago when leading at Charlton. The barrier is sticky, but he is the type of horse who can sometimes make his own luck. ZEUSS (5) is an interesting runner here. He is fourth-up for Rebecca Bartley and is having his first look at the Melton track. He has flashed home to win his last two starts impressively. An awkward barrier, but his last two starts have also been from tricky starting positions. KIMCHI (4) has been in great form recently, racing at his best and putting together good performances. This is harder, though. BACK: HIGHVIEW HAMMER (2)– 2.5 units (win) SELECTIONS: HIGHVIEW HAMMER (2), SPORTS WRACK (6), ZEUSS (5), KIMCHI (4)

OVERVIEW:TED BEAR (7) has a great turn of foot when he is saved for one run. His race map is likely to be tricky here from the sticky barrier, but he’s a nice horse who is racing well. AUSSIE JAY MAC (8) is the only horse on the second row, so he has options with his race map. However, there are some concerns with his manners, as he has occasionally galloped in his runs. He seems to be okay when he’s in front, which he won’t be here from barrier eight. LIBERTY STAR DUST (6) was a good second last start at Cranbourne. He worked forward, raced in the breeze and battled on well for second. He will need some luck here from the barrier. TOMBEUR (1) looks to be a smart performer who is still learning what racing is all about. He’s had three career starts. He won on debut, then had to race tough in his second start but still ran well for fourth. Last start, he got it wrong with his manners. If he does everything right and can hold a forward position, he’s a big threat from the fence. SELECTIONS: TED BEAR (7), AUSSIE JAY MAC (8), LIBERTY STAR DUST (6), TOMBEUR (1)

OVERVIEW:TEX GOES BANG (7) finished fifth last start, beaten 8.5 metres. However, he was racing in the breeze and covered an extra 31 metres by being off the fence. This race looks a little easier. He will need some luck, but James Herbertson takes the reins. He’s the best driver in Australia and knows how to find luck. MISSMALACHITE (8) is ultra-consistent and has only missed a place once in her last seven starts. She has map options as the only horse on the back row and will be flashing home here. NORTHERN TERROR (2) ran a good third last start. He settled near last, made a three-wide run and raced in the breeze, covering an extra 26 metres off the fence. He was beaten only three metres. Barrier two suits. STELLAR QUEEN (3) rarely runs a bad race, although she’s only won three times in her long career. She will need some luck, but she can run home well if saved for one run. SELECTIONS: TEX GOES BANG (7), MISSMALACHITE (8), NORTHERN TERROR (2), STELLAR QUEEN (3)

OVERVIEW:MAJOR MAURIE (5) was smashing the line impressively last start, first-up for John and Ewa Justice, but was just held up and left it too late to win. It appeared to be an improved performance and I’m looking for him to race well again here. JILLIBY UTAH (3) led and won well to break through for his maiden victory at Melton last start in rain-affected conditions. With the right run, he can run a good race again here, now with the winning confidence. ALCATRAZ GIRL (1) doesn't have great numerical form, but she has the gate speed to map well here from the ace. LIVERMERE (4) is a consistent mare who is racing well. She does have good gate speed, which she may opt to use here, or she could save her speed for one run at the end. BACK: MAJOR MAURIE (5)– 3 units (win) SELECTIONS: MAJOR MAURIE (5), JILLIBY UTAH (3), ALCATRAZ GIRL (1), LIVERMERE (4)

OVERVIEW: What a cracking race this is, one you often see on a Saturday night. Top free-for-all pacer YAMBUKIAN (6) is fourth-up here after more than a year on the sidelines, so he will be close to reaching peak race fitness. He was a brilliant second to Fox Dan in 1.51.5 two starts ago, narrowly beaten. He ran a good fourth last start in the Casey Classic in a race that was fence-dominated, while he was racing off the fence. He is class. MADIGAN (4) is a smart performer. He finished fourth last start in the St Arnaud Pacing Cup. He got home well after being held up. The map is a bit awkward, as he has some gate speed, but not as much as some of the horses around him. ISOLATION (3) was a brilliant second last start at massive odds behind Derby winner Dynamite Dan. He has great gate speed and is in career-best form. THUNDERFIRE (2) is a lightly raced horse whose talent has seen him step up to this class quite quickly. He will need some luck here, but he has ability. He may need some time to adjust to racing at this level. SELECTIONS: YAMBUKIAN (6), MADIGAN (4), ISOLATION (3), THUNDERFIRE (2) Harness.org.au Help Privacy Advertise Terms Of Use Contact Us © Racing Information Services Enterprise 2026 Powered by

REACH THE PEAK (5) has won his last three starts and he is racing in career best form at the moment. He was a dominant winner at Globe Derby on Saturday night when he defeated ALORA by 1.9 metres after facing the breeze. ALORA (1) does race well here at Port Pirie and she will love the inside draw today. PLACES YOU DONT (7) and ROCKNROLL SPIRIT (3) are also chances.

SWEET NICKY (5) didn’t work into the race at Globe Derby on Saturday night but her run before that at Port Pirie was strong. She has the speed to lead today and if she does lead then she will be hard to catch. MY ULTIMATE BANJO (8) looks like a big danger after an impressive win at Globe Derby last start. MANDS PEARL (7) and BROBENAH GIRL (4) are also chances.

TREACHEROUS DAN (7) should end up on the leaders back from the inside of the second row. His record is strong and he looks too good for this field today. MICKTHEBESTBUTCHER (1), IN THE SUMMERTIME (4) and WHENIMREADY (9) are also chances.
